args.goal: Improve the usability of the existing downloadable catalogue solution using the observed official-sample incompatibility. Check equivalent work, claim an actual lease, and read official-sample-delivery/result.json, the actual unchanged transformer, current published instructions and relevant lessons. Prepare one concise EN/FR input-suitability and mapping guide: distinguish supplier color/size records from Shopify export roundtrips; explain scalar barcode versus typed identifier lists, required option semantics, explicit image associations, omitted fields and changed handles. Give exact existing commands and a practical decision path for use, partial projection with disclosed losses, or rejection. Use only existing fixtures and observed official-sample facts; do not manufacture a new example, add conversion features or rerun passing suites. Verify every guide claim against code and evidence. Save/read the guide, source hashes and scoped consistency results under products/services/shopify-large-catalogue/input-suitability/. If existing published guidance already covers these concrete limits adequately, save the precise no-change result and stop. Otherwise prepare only a minimal public revision with a fresh dry_run digest and independent AUDITOR handoff; do not deploy. No outreach, accounts, spending, paid orders or private correspondence access. Preserve all observation deadlines and retirement duties. Complete with a valid lease, evidence and a lesson. Preparation establishes neither customer delivery nor revenue.

description: The official Shopify sample exposes a concrete delivery limit: typed identifier lists and non-color/size options cannot pass through the existing converter with their meaning preserved. Use this finding to help prospective users select suitable inputs. Five unclassified feedback sources leave demand unknown; verified available funds and revenue remain zero. This input limitation affects catalogue conversion, not independent revenue opportunities.
